requirements.source: inference — the frozen API replaces whole documents by merge patch with no precondition, while the operator, agents and the controller all write tasks; Plane writes of a pod on old code overwrote three specs during the 2026-11-08 import.

requirements.title: Authorized idempotent commands
requirements.statement: Non-idempotent create/trigger commands require idempotency keys scoped by stable authority principal, workspace and action and bound to normalized arguments, targets and expected revisions. Retention and expiry are declared; execution and replay both recheck current authority.
acceptance: AC1: Same key/payload returns the recorded operation after current authorization checks.
AC2: Different payload under one key returns409 idempotency_key_conflict.
AC3: Lost-response recovery reads the operation receipt before issuing a new key; expired transport replay never promises indefinite exactly-once effects.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: State changes are named actions
requirements.statement:
`PATCH` edits fields and never changes state or queue status. Each transition is its own
endpoint (`POST …/tasks/{id}/release`, `/requeue`, `/cancel`, `/hand-back/resolve`,
`/decisions/{id}/answer`, …) with its own roles and its required reason fields.
acceptance: AC1: A `PATCH` containing `state` is rejected with 422 naming the action to use.
requirements.source: spec NOTES "API conventions".

requirements.title: Server-assigned ids, client-supplied external ids
requirements.statement:
The server assigns ids and sequence numbers. A client may supply an `external_id` unique within
a project, which makes creates idempotent and lets a file be re-applied.
acceptance: AC1: Creating two tasks with the same `external_id` in one project yields one task.
AC2: No operation requires the client to invent a primary key.
requirements.source: spec NOTES API ambiguity 10 ("`POST` takes the whole object with a client-chosen `id`") — a gap in the frozen spec, not in the estate: Plane assigns ids and sequence numbers today, and `plane_tasks.py file` re-applies a file by task id.

requirements.title: Authorized resumable event feeds
requirements.statement: Event feeds expose durable cursor-based authorized observations with at-least-once delivery, stable event IDs, per-owner/workspace order, declared retention and filter binding. Cross-service timelines use causal links and observed times, not invented global commit order.
acceptance: AC1: Reconnect/replay can duplicate events but stable IDs permit deduplication without loss within retention.
AC2: An expired cursor returns410 retention_gap with an authorized snapshot/resync route.
AC3: Membership/permission revocation affects resumed and open streams within the declared bound.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Outbound webhooks
requirements.statement:
An operator can register webhook endpoints for event kinds. Deliveries are signed (HMAC-SHA256
over the body with a per-endpoint secret, timestamped), retried with backoff, and logged with
their outcome. Destinations are checked against private, loopback and link-local ranges unless
explicitly allowed.
acceptance: AC1: A receiver can verify signature and timestamp from the documentation alone.
AC2: A webhook pointed at a metadata address or a cluster-internal service is refused by default.
requirements.source: DESIGN §7 ("Webhooks/events out"); Plane benchmark (signed webhooks; nine SSRF advisories — see [12-quality-bar.md](12-quality-bar.md)).

requirements.title: Rate limiting
requirements.statement:
Requests are rate-limited per token and per session; over-limit requests get 429 with
`Retry-After`. Limits are configuration.
acceptance: AC1: Default limits never throttle the bundled console or CLI in the scenario suite.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (API key limit default 60/minute); conductor `causes.tick` polls each parked item at most every 30 minutes "for Plane's rate limit".

requirements.title: Bounded responses and an explicit redaction contract
requirements.statement:
No endpoint returns an unbounded collection. Overview and list responses are built from field
allowlists and never include packets, prompts, check commands, free-form worker facts, tokens or
secrets. Detail endpoints that expose sensitive material (a packet, a trace) are separate
operations with their own role.
acceptance: AC1: A test enumerates every list and overview schema and asserts none references a sensitive field.
AC2: Response size for any list call is bounded independently of history size.
requirements.source: FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN "Decision and boundary" and "Source model and invariants"; harness-console decided D10.

requirements.title: Unknown is not zero
requirements.statement:
Every aggregate carries `as_of` and a coverage state. A value whose source is unread, stale or
incomplete is `null` with a `reason`; a ratio with a zero denominator is `null` with
`no_eligible_items`, never a number.
acceptance: AC1: Shared helper and a lint: aggregate fields are typed as `value | null + reason`.
AC2: The UI renders `unknown` for null (UI-024).
requirements.source: FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN ("They must not be rendered as zero while unconnected"); harness-console J1; factory-measurement-contract "Sources, windows, and missingness".

requirements.title: Stability and deprecation
requirements.statement:
At 1.0 the `/v1` API is frozen: only additive changes within the major. A deprecation is
announced in the changelog and by a `Deprecation` header and stays for at least two minor
releases or six months, whichever is longer. CI checks every PR for breaking changes against the
last released OpenAPI document.
acceptance: AC1: A PR that removes a field or tightens a type fails the compatibility job.
AC2: Before 1.0, each minor's breaking changes are listed in its upgrade notes.
requirements.source: CORPUS M6.3 ("API backward-compatibility checks against the published OpenAPI"); Plane benchmark (no written deprecation policy found in the repo).

requirements.title: Truthful health and runtime identity
requirements.statement: Liveness is process health; readiness verifies the supported Appwrite endpoint/project, authenticated runtime access, required schema/index readiness and mandatory role capabilities. Runtime identity exposes deployed source/version and implemented capability manifest without needing cluster access.
acceptance: AC1: A wrong project/session or missing required index/permission fails readiness.
AC2: An unavailable optional connector is visible and does not masquerade as an empty successful response.
AC3: The capability manifest belongs to the running revision, independently of planned design operations.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: The running revision is visible only as a cluster annotation (task-pickup conformance row 7, HARNESS-256; BL-28).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Transaction-budget-aware bulk work
requirements.statement: Bulk filing reports the configured atomic limit and supports resumable import operations beyond it. The backend accounts for task, relation, receipt, audit and event writes; the advertised number of tasks is not the transaction operation budget.
acceptance: AC1: The largest supported atomic batch commits completely or rolls back.
AC2: A request exceeding that budget is refused or explicitly converted to a resumable operation.
AC3: Partial import progress and failures are observable in UI, REST, MCP and CLI.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Inbound Git host webhooks are an accelerator, not a dependency
requirements.statement:
Sortyard works by polling the Git host. If inbound webhooks are configured, they only shorten
the time to observe a fact; every fact is still confirmed by reading it. Webhook payloads are
verified by signature.
acceptance: AC1: The full scenario suite passes with webhooks disabled.
AC2: A forged webhook changes nothing.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "The rule" (observed state); the estate today polls (`drive` every 3 min, `plane_sync` every 5 min) and cannot receive webhooks on a tailnet-only host.

requirements.title: Operator requests and fenced system transitions
requirements.statement: Operator-facing actions request release, repair, requeue or promotion through the public API; system-only claiming/advancement and landing execute behind controller/integrator fencing. A client cannot assert a system actor. Internal protocol endpoints, if any, are separately authenticated and excluded from operator discovery.
acceptance: AC1: A delegated operator can request every action allowed to that operator.
AC2: A worker or forged actor header cannot claim, advance another attempt or instruct landing.
AC3: Public tool discovery contains no callable system-only transition.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Scoped workspaces and collaboration profiles
requirements.statement: Resource identities, queries, graph edges, cache keys, events and credentials include installation/workspace/project scope. Individual collaborators in one workspace ship first; independent operations/workspaces are a supported target with explicit isolation qualification, not an assumed guarantee from a field.
acceptance: AC1: Two projects in one workspace enforce membership and delegated scopes.
AC2: A distinct workspace cannot be inferred through search, events, exports or relationships.
AC3: An unqualified independent-workspace profile reports unavailable with its missing setup/proof rather than enabling unsafe tenancy.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: MCP over HTTP from the API service, plus a stdio shim
requirements.statement:
The API service serves MCP over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, authenticated by the same tokens as
REST. `sortyardctl mcp` is a stdio shim for clients that only speak stdio. Both expose the same
tools.
acceptance: AC1: A remote agent with a URL and a token lists and calls tools with no local install.
AC2: Redirects are never followed with a token attached.
requirements.source: the prototype is stdio only (`clients/mcp_server.py`); legacy `cp_mcp.py` (HTTP, protocol versions 2025-03-26 to 2025-11-25).

requirements.title: Discoverable domain tool packs
requirements.statement: Role/domain tool packs keep the active tool list small; every authorized implemented operation remains discoverable through paginated generic describe/call operations. Planned, uninstalled, unavailable and forbidden operations are distinguished.
acceptance: AC1: An operator agent can discover governance and integration actions beyond the task tools.
AC2: No generic tool bypasses action authorization or names an arbitrary backend URL.
AC3: A missing backend capability returns a specific unavailable reason.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: Agents operate the legacy system with the scripts of CLI-005, which need a shell in the cluster and the shared board key; its MCP server is read-only with four tools (driver §4 "Tools"; `cp_mcp.py`; BL-20, BL-26).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Full reach through three generic tools
requirements.statement:
Every API operation the token may call is reachable through `list_operations`,
`describe_operation` and `call_operation`. This is how "APIs for everything, for agents" holds
without hundreds of tools.
acceptance: AC1: Parity test: for each role, the operations reachable through MCP equal the role's column of the permission matrix.
requirements.source: DESIGN §7; `clients/README.md` parity rule ("every API operation is exactly one MCP tool").

requirements.title: Bounded, honest tool results
requirements.statement:
Tool results are capped (default 48,000 characters) with a continuation cursor, say `unknown`
where the API returned null with a reason, and carry MCP annotations (`readOnlyHint`,
`destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`). A refusal from the API is passed back unchanged.
acceptance: AC1: A result over the cap is truncated at a record boundary and names how to continue.
requirements.source: `cp_mcp.py` (`MAX_RESULT_CHARS` 48,000; "A source reported unknown/unavailable is unknown, not zero").

requirements.title: Worker tools are the stage contract
requirements.statement:
A stage token can do two things: read its own packet and submit its own result. Both are
available as REST operations and as MCP tools.
acceptance: AC1: A stage token calling any other operation gets 403; calling another stage's packet gets 404.
requirements.source: DESIGN §7 ("a build worker can read its own context packet and submit its own stage result — nothing else").

requirements.title: `sortyardctl`
requirements.statement:
One CLI, installable with `pipx` and shipped in the image. Configuration: API URL and token from
environment, a profile file, or `--token-file`; a token is never accepted as an argument. Exit
codes: 0 success, 1 refused by the API, 2 usage, 3 unreachable.
acceptance: AC1: `sortyardctl --help` works offline and lists every command.
AC2: The process list never shows a token.
requirements.source: `clients/README.md` (`SORTYARD_API_URL`, `SORTYARD_TOKEN`, exit codes).

requirements.title: Commands for the things people and agents actually do
requirements.statement:
Task-level commands with readable output and `--json`: `task file|add|get|list|edit|move|note`,
`pickup status`, `queue`, `why`, `requeue`, `cancel`, `job run`, `decision list|answer`,
`needs list|discharge`, `lanes get|set`, `pause`, `resume`, `apply`, `export`, `audit`,
`health`, `backup`. Commands arrive with the capability they operate.
acceptance: AC1: Each command maps to exactly one documented sequence of API calls.
AC2: Human output and `--json` output are both covered by snapshot tests.
requirements.source: driver §4 "Tools", §7 "Common operations".

requirements.title: Every API operation is reachable
requirements.statement:
`sortyardctl api <operationId> [--param k=v] [--body JSON|@file|-]` calls any operation. A parity
test fails if an operation has no CLI path.
acceptance: AC1: Unknown operations or arguments send nothing.
requirements.source: `clients/README.md` parity rule; DESIGN §7 ("everything the CLI does is an API call (no back doors)").

requirements.title: Dry run
requirements.statement:
Mutating task-level commands accept `--dry-run` and print what would change, using the server's
own evaluation.
acceptance: AC1: `task file --dry-run` returns the verdict each task would get and writes nothing.
requirements.source: `drive.py --dry-run`, `plane_sync.py --dry-run`.

requirements.title: Parity with the legacy operator tools
acceptance: AC1: The migration guide has this table and each row has a test.

AC2: Coverage of the legacy operations inventory (BL-20: the tools above, the legacy console's journeys and the steering done on the Plane board), as the share with a documented and tested Sortyard equivalent. Target: 100% by the MS5 gate. Floor: 100% of the operations the usage census (MIG-017) shows in use, before the first cutover.
requirements.source: driver §4 "Tools"; conductor README (tool descriptions).

measured.target: 100% by the MS5 gate.
measured.floor: 100% of the operations the usage census (MIG-017) shows in use, before the first cutover.

requirements.title: Appwrite-backed first-run administrator binding
requirements.statement: Bootstrap binds a verified Appwrite user to the first installation admin using a one-time, expiring setup grant. It creates no separate password database, default password or shared admin token.
acceptance: AC1: A setup grant cannot be reused or applied by an unverified identity.
AC2: Later administrators are granted through explicit authorized membership/domain actions.
AC3: Setup status identifies missing substrate configuration without exposing secrets.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Appwrite human identity and sessions
requirements.statement: Use the supported self-hosted Appwrite Account/session/JWT and Teams capabilities selected in SY-DEC-004. Resolve users by issuer/project/user ID. Alternative providers flow through supported Appwrite identity; no new local password store or trusted raw proxy identity is required.
acceptance: AC1: Invalid/expired sessions and forged identity headers are refused.
AC2: Pending invitations grant no project access.
AC3: Cloud OAuth-server/installation features are not advertised without a verified supported installation.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: The legacy console trusts a `Tailscale-User-Login` header that pods inside the cluster can forge, and its mutation routes accept any same-network POST (harness-console decided D2, D16; VISION; BL-26).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Session and request hardening
requirements.statement:
Cookie sessions are `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, with CSRF protection; mutations require
a same-origin request with a JSON body. Token-authenticated requests need no CSRF. The console
ships a strict Content-Security-Policy.
acceptance: AC1: A cross-site form post to any mutation is rejected.
AC2: A security-headers test runs against every route.
requirements.source: harness-console VISION ("mutation routes accept any same-network POST"), decided D2.

requirements.title: Scoped human roles and explicit delegation
requirements.statement: Viewer, operator and admin apply only within granted workspace/project/installation scope and registered service capabilities. An Appwrite Team owner is not installation-admin; no human grant implicitly confers system-executor identity, backend root credentials or another application authority.
acceptance: AC1: The published permission matrix distinguishes membership, domain actions and system-only execution.
AC2: Project-admin cannot grant workspace/installation rights or another project scope.
AC3: Delegated rights intersect the live human grant and resource policy.
requirements.source: PERMISSIONS.md; DESIGN §3.9.
requirements.amendment_reason: Latest owner scope, single-authority integration and existing testing/governance doctrine

requirements.title: Service accounts and tokens
requirements.statement:
A service account has a role and a scope. Tokens are shown once, stored hashed, expire (default
90 days), can be revoked, and record last use. Issuing, rotating and revoking are audited.
acceptance: AC1: A database dump contains no usable token.
AC2: An expiring token is flagged in the token list ahead of expiry (default 14 days) and, from MS5, raises an attention item (OBS-014).
requirements.source: `identity/README.md` (scopes issued and revoked as data, every mutation audited); the owner's GitHub token expiry is tracked by hand today (driver §5).

requirements.title: Purpose-bound accounts and operator delegation
requirements.statement: Separate autonomous intake/grooming/sensor/worker service accounts from agents delegated by an operator. Delegated agents can use the operator action surface under the intersection of issuer authority, resource policy and explicit scope/action/expiry restrictions.
acceptance: AC1: A delegated operator may create tasks and propose permitted policy changes through their normal gates.
AC2: A narrow worker cannot introduce arbitrary work, impersonate a system actor or self-widen its grant.
AC3: Issuer removal, expiry or revocation invalidates delegated rights within the declared bound.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Stage tokens
requirements.statement:
The controller mints one token per stage attempt, confined to that attempt and its chain epoch,
expiring at the stage deadline plus a margin, and revoked when the stage ends.
acceptance: AC1: A stage token used after its stage ended is refused.
requirements.source: `identity/README.md` ("a build-worker token, confined to one `stage_run_id`").

requirements.title: Independent execution gates without disabling operator agency
requirements.statement: No model-driven principal may self-claim work, become the controller/integrator or bypass independent execution/release gates. Operator delegation preserves actions that the human may legitimately perform, including task creation and allowed governance changes; sensitive authorization changes retain their own authority requirements.
acceptance: AC1: Across simultaneous grants a worker cannot accumulate forbidden create-plus-claim or system authority.
AC2: The same authorized operator action has the same outcome through UI and delegated-agent transport.
AC3: A policy edit does not give the editing agent direct claim/landing authority.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: The sync that files urgent triage items and the driver that claims them share one Plane key (DESIGN §7; `plane_sync.queue_triage`); by inference the filing tools use the same one (BL-26).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Authorisation is central, default-deny and object-scoped
requirements.statement:
One authorisation function decides every request from the operation's declared roles and the
caller's bindings. An operation with no declared role is unreachable. Object access is scoped in
the data-access layer: every query is constrained by the caller's workspace and project scope,
so an id from another scope behaves as not found.
acceptance: AC1: No handler contains its own role check (lint).
AC2: A request for an object outside the caller's scope returns 404, never 403 with details and never the object.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark — 57 of 89 published advisories are authorisation flaws (CWE-639, 862, 284, 863); see [12-quality-bar.md](12-quality-bar.md).

requirements.title: The authorisation matrix is tested cell by cell
requirements.statement:
For every operation × role there is an automated test asserting allow or deny, generated from
the matrix; and for every operation that takes an object id, a test that an id from another
project and another workspace is refused.
acceptance: AC1: Adding an operation without declaring its roles fails CI.
AC2: The generated suite runs on every PR in under two minutes.
requirements.source: `test_openapi.py` already checks the matrix document against the spec; this extends the check to the running service.

requirements.title: Audit log
requirements.statement:
Every mutation records actor, time, target, before and after (redacted), request id, client and
result, in an append-only store. A refused request is logged separately from mutations. The
audit trail of an object is visible on that object.
acceptance: AC1: The append-only guarantee is enforced by the database (update, delete and truncate refused), as in the existing migration.
AC2: The time from a mutating UI action to its entry in the entity's audit trail. Target: 1 s. Floor: 5 s.
requirements.source: harness-console J5 ("an audit entry (actor, time, target, result) is visible on the entity"); migration `0001` (refuse triggers).

requirements.title: Standing delegation and exact optional approvals
requirements.statement: Standing delegation allows routine authorized actions without per-action human confirmation. Where policy requires approval, it binds the normalized plan hash, target revision, authority and expiry; edits invalidate approval. Proposer, authority principal, executor and approver are separately audited. A required approval is a Decision with decision_kind=action_plan_approval and immutable plan binding. decision.answer approves or rejects that exact plan through the public action contract; preparing an edit supersedes the prior plan and invalidates its approval. Approval Decisions inherit the plan workspace and optional project scope; a workspace action needs no invented project and cannot be approved by a project-only grant.
acceptance: AC1: An agent action within standing scope executes without an invented extra approval.
AC2: A changed/stale plan cannot reuse an approval.
AC3: Silence or an expired decision cannot grant credential, public, spending or irreversible authority.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).

requirements.title: The console is a client of the public API
requirements.statement:
A single-page app served as static files by the API service. It uses only public API operations
and the event stream. There is no console-only endpoint.
acceptance: AC1: A test serves the console against a mock built from the OpenAPI document alone and every route renders.
AC2: A lint forbids request paths outside the generated API client.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 rule; SY-DEC-001 (Vite SPA, static files served by the API service).

requirements.title: UI-for-everything is measured
requirements.statement:
Operations are annotated `operator-facing` in the OpenAPI document. A coverage manifest maps
each to the route and control that invokes it. CI fails when an operator-facing operation has no
UI path, unless it carries a dated exemption.
acceptance: AC1: Coverage of operator-facing operations by a console control, from the manifest check. Target: 100% at every merge to `main`, with no exemption. Floor: 100% at each milestone exit for the operations introduced in that milestone or earlier.
AC2: The manifest is published as a docs page ("where is X in the UI").
requirements.source: Joe's objective ("there is a UI for everything"); CORPUS M5.6 defers every write surface to Phase 5 — see CF-03.

measured.target: 100% at every merge to `main`, with no exemption.
measured.floor: 100% at each milestone exit for the operations introduced in that milestone or earlier.

requirements.title: Board and list
requirements.statement:
The board shows tasks in columns by state; the list shows them in rows. Both support filters
(TRK-014), reordering of top-level tasks by drag or keyboard (TRK-007), and inline display of
park and hand-back reasons. Dragging changes rank only; state and priority are changed from the
item.
acceptance: AC1: Every drag has a keyboard equivalent and an undo.
AC2: The time from a drag to every open board and list showing the new order, without a reload. Target: 1 s. Floor: 5 s.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 1 ("Dragging is defined, not magic"); task-ready ("To reorder delivery, drag top-level tasks on the board").

requirements.title: Task detail is one timeline
requirements.statement:
One page per task: fields and spec, relations, the filing verdict and reasons, and one ordered
timeline of notes, state changes, decisions and — from MS3 — the chain: stages with attempts,
durations and outcomes, the change request, checks, review verdicts, usage. There is no separate
"pipeline" record to click through to.
acceptance: AC1: From a task, the stage outcome that explains its current state is on the same page (zero navigation).
AC2: Every timeline entry has a stable deep link.

AC3: Demonstration (benchmark, MS3) — from a task, a scripted operator finds the stage outcome that explains its current state, on Sortyard and on the legacy pair. Target: zero navigation, shown within 1 s of opening the task. Floor: fewer steps than the legacy route across two tools (BL-18).
requirements.source: DESIGN §6.0 ("A task's detail *is* its chain"); Joe 2026-11-06 (the dashboard "connects tickets with the pipeline").
requirements.baseline: The ticket is in Plane and its runs are in the harness console: two tools with separate navigation (DESIGN §0; Joe 2026-11-06, the dashboard should connect "tickets with the pipeline"; BL-18).

measured.target: zero navigation, shown within 1 s of opening the task.
measured.floor: fewer steps than the legacy route across two tools (BL-18).

requirements.title: Creating and editing tasks
requirements.statement:
A form for the tracker fields and the typed spec with inline readiness feedback, a raw YAML view
of the same spec, and paste-or-upload of a task file with a per-task verdict preview before
filing.
acceptance: AC1: Form and YAML views round-trip without loss.
AC2: Readiness errors appear as the user types, from the server's evaluation.
requirements.source: task-ready "The task item"; `plane_tasks.py file`.

requirements.title: Pickup Preview and "why"
requirements.statement:
Per project: the queue in claim order, slot holders with phase and age, the reason code for
every task not claimable now, and the next-N simulation. On every task detail page: a "why is
this not running" panel with the same reasons and the tasks ranked ahead.
acceptance: AC1: Each reason code links to its documentation and, where an operator can fix it, to the control that does.
AC2: The view states the evaluation time and the policy versions it used.
requirements.source: task-pickup §7 (the "Where a reader sees it" column); HARNESS-251, HARNESS-256.

requirements.title: Owner list and decision inbox
requirements.statement:
One view of everything waiting on a person, grouped by route: decisions with their default and
time left, escalated premise-class decisions, needs routed to the viewer's route, items escalated
to a person. Decisions are answered here.
acceptance: AC1: Answering a decision records the chosen value and the route that will apply it.
AC2: A decision past its date that took its default shows as such, not as open.
requirements.source: driver §6 (the owner "answers `decision` items; defaults apply on their date"); conductor README (depends-on-Joe list, `needs-human`, `route:owner`).

requirements.title: Lanes and tuning
requirements.statement:
Edit lanes per project, pause and resume, admission caps and the scheduling policy values, with
the current value, the default, who last changed it and when. Saving shows the diff and its
effect on the Pickup Preview before it applies.
acceptance: AC1: A lane change needs no deploy and no file edit.
AC2: Every value shows the legacy constant it replaces where there is one (DEF-005).
requirements.source: driver §1 (knobs in `repos.yaml`, hardcoded copies in three files); DESIGN §5.3.

requirements.title: Overview: glance at the floor
requirements.statement:
The landing page: health state and what drives it; per project running, waiting, parked and
handed-back counts with oldest ages; slots and heavy-cap use; recent merges; the attention list.
It updates live.
acceptance: AC1: A source that is unknown or stale renders `unknown`, never 0.
AC2: Every number links to the list that produces it.
AC3: Render time of the Overview on the reference fixture. Target: 500 ms. Floor: 2 s, the legacy console's bar for the same journey.
requirements.source: harness-console J1; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN "Screen and feedback loop".

measured.floor: 2 s, the legacy console's bar for the same journey.

requirements.title: Chains and actions
requirements.statement:
For a chain: the stage timeline with attempts, durations, the reason a stage is waiting or
failed, and the binding. Actions — requeue, cancel, stop, resume — are offered only where the
API says they are legal, behind a dialog that states the effect; the result and its audit entry
appear inline.
acceptance: AC1: An action the API would refuse is not offered.
AC2: A run detail page never returns an error for an existing run; ids are unique.
requirements.source: harness-console J3, J5; VISION ("run detail currently 502s").

requirements.title: Logs and traces
acceptance: AC1: Opening a 5 MB log or trace. Target: first lines within 300 ms and no frame over 50 ms while scrolling. Floor: no frame over 200 ms (frame budget asserted in the e2e test).
requirements.source: harness-console J3; DESIGN §6 view 4.

measured.target: first lines within 300 ms and no frame over 50 ms while scrolling.
measured.floor: no frame over 200 ms (frame budget asserted in the e2e test).

requirements.title: Credentials
requirements.statement:
Accounts and keys with health, expiry and last use; add and re-authenticate through a stepper
that survives refresh and navigation, shows progress on slow steps, retries transient errors and
can be cancelled. Values are never shown and never entered except through the provider's own
flow or a paste-once field.
acceptance: AC1: Viewing the page triggers no paid probe.
AC2: A stuck flow can be cancelled for any provider.
requirements.source: harness-console J4; console routes `credentials`, components `add-account`, `sign-in`.

requirements.title: Parked and self-heal queues
requirements.statement:
Lists of parked and handed-back work with reason, blocking cause, age and what would bring each
back; the resolution actions of the self-heal contract (REC-009).
acceptance: AC1: Items older than the self-heal drain limit (default 24 h) are marked and match the `SELF-HEAL-STALLED` condition's list.
requirements.source: conductor README "Self-heal drain", "Blocking causes".

requirements.title: Health
acceptance: AC1: A silent mechanism is findable from the Overview in two clicks.
requirements.source: MECHANISMS.md; `GET /api/mh/factory/mechanisms`.

requirements.title: Evidence-backed ecosystem dashboards
requirements.statement: Project and portfolio dashboards derive throughput, blockers, delivery, cost, policy, membership and integration health from authorized records with observed_at, coverage and evidence links. Appwrite is the native substrate; optional external observability is not required for core dashboards.
acceptance: AC1: Unknown/partial source coverage is shown rather than counted as zero.
AC2: A person and delegated agent receive the same metric definition and accessible source references.
AC3: A dashboard value can be reproduced from its retained input/version window.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Decision log and audit explorers
requirements.statement:
Search scheduling decisions by task, reason code, time and policy version, and open one
evaluation to see its inputs; browse the audit log by actor, object and time. A basic version
ships in MS2; saved searches and replay of an evaluation are complete by MS6.
acceptance: AC1: "Why was X not claimed at T" is answerable from the UI without the CLI.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 (DecisionLog explorer); harness-console `audit-trail` component.

requirements.title: Administration
requirements.statement:
Users, role bindings, service accounts and tokens; projects and repositories with an onboarding
wizard; system information (version, schema, image digest). Integrations, definitions and backup
controls join as their capabilities land; the page is complete at MS6 .
acceptance: AC1: A new project can be created and its first task filed without leaving the UI.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 12; onboarding.md (today: edit `repos.yaml`, push, wait for the onboarding check).

requirements.title: Performance budgets
requirements.statement:
The console keeps a normalised local store fed by the event stream, applies an operator's change
optimistically and reconciles with the server's answer, so that no action waits for a round trip
before it shows. Initial JavaScript is budgeted and enforced in CI. Grids are virtualised (about
50 rows mounted) and scroll 10,000 fixture rows smoothly. Lists use server cursors. Route code
is lazy-loaded and the next likely route is preloaded.
acceptance: AC1: Initial JavaScript, gzipped, enforced by the budget check. Target: 200 KB. Floor: 350 KB, the legacy console's budget.
AC2: An e2e test asserts the mounted-row bound on a 10,000-row fixture.

AC3: Interaction latency on the reference workload, from an input (click, key, end of a drag) to its visible result and from a route change to its content. Target: p95 at most 100 ms for an input and 200 ms for a route change. Floor: p95 at most 1 s, and no journey slower than on the legacy console (BL-18).
AC4: First load on a cold cache, to interactive, on the reference connection. Target: 1 s. Floor: 2 s.
AC5: An optimistic change that the server refuses is rolled back visibly, with the reason.
requirements.source: `console/check_budget.py` (`BUDGET_BYTES = 350 * 1024`); harness-console J2; decided D4. The local store and optimistic updates are a design change made on 2026-11-12 to reach the latency target (inference: a round trip for every action cannot meet it).

measured.floor: 350 KB, the legacy console's budget.

measured.target: p95 at most 100 ms for an input and 200 ms for a route change.
measured.floor: p95 at most 1 s, and no journey slower than on the legacy console (BL-18).

requirements.title: Accessibility
requirements.statement:
Target WCAG 2.2 AA. CI runs an automated accessibility scan on every route with zero serious or
critical violations, and every journey test is also run keyboard-only. Focus is managed on route
change and in dialogs; live updates are announced politely.
acceptance: AC1: The accessibility and keyboard specs are required checks.
AC2: Colour is never the only carrier of state.
requirements.source: harness-console journeys preamble ("keyboard-only, with zero serious/critical axe violations"); `console/e2e/tests/a11y.spec.ts`, `keyboard.spec.ts`; components `route-focus`, `announce`.

requirements.title: Responsive
requirements.statement: Every journey passes at 390, 834 and 1440 pixels wide.
acceptance: AC1: The e2e matrix runs the journeys at the three widths.
requirements.source: harness-console journeys preamble; VISION ("on a laptop or a phone").

requirements.title: Live without reload
requirements.statement:
Views update from the event stream, falling back to polling. A stale or disconnected view says
so.
acceptance: AC1: Killing the stream connection shows a "reconnecting" state and recovers without a reload.
requirements.source: harness-console J1; decided D5; console `lib/live.ts`.

requirements.title: Command palette
requirements.statement: A keyboard palette jumps to any task, chain or run by id or text and runs common actions.
acceptance: AC1: Typing `ROVE-12` and Enter opens that task from any page.
requirements.source: harness-console J2 ("⌘K palette jumps to any request/chain/run by id"); console `command-palette` component.

requirements.title: Design tokens and brand
requirements.statement: One token set (colour, type, spacing) with light and dark themes, using the Sortyard brand kit.
acceptance: AC1: No component hard-codes a colour.
requirements.source: meta-harness `projects/sortyard/branding/`; harness-console decided D3.

requirements.title: Empty, error and unknown states are designed
requirements.statement:
Every view has a designed state for: nothing yet, loading, failed to load, and value unknown.
An absent value is never rendered as zero, a blank or a spinner that never ends.
acceptance: AC1: Storybook (or equivalent) has a story per state per view, and the e2e suite visits the failed and unknown states.
requirements.source: AGENTS.md "Testing model" (one story per machine state; every gate defines its absent state); harness-console J1.

requirements.title: Strings are externalised; English only
requirements.statement:
All user-visible strings go through a message catalogue with locale-aware dates and numbers.
1.0 ships English only and documents how a locale is added.
acceptance: AC1: A lint fails on a hard-coded user-visible string in a component.
AC2: A pseudo-locale build renders every route without clipped or missing text.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (22 locales, an i18n sync check in CI); see [12-quality-bar.md](12-quality-bar.md) for the stance.

requirements.title: Embedded concierge
requirements.statement:
The console keeps the embedded concierge of the existing console: ask a question, get an answer
grounded in live state with citations, and approve proposed actions (IAM-012). It is a client of
the operator-agent tools (MCP-002) with the signed-in operator's permissions, it has no private
endpoint, and it is off until a model credential is configured for it. Its ambient half, the
attention list, ships in MS5 (OBS-014).
acceptance: AC1: The legacy concierge journeys (J6, and the second concierge journey of J12) pass against Sortyard.
AC2: Every statement the concierge makes about state cites the record it came from; text from tasks, logs and traces is treated as data, never as instructions.
AC3: With no model credential the entry point says how to enable it, and nothing else in the console changes.
AC4: Time to the first token of an answer on the reference workload. Target: 1 s. Floor: no slower than the legacy concierge (BL-18).
requirements.source: harness-console J6–J8, decided D7–D9, D14–D15; console `components/concierge/*`, `concierge.py`; e2e `j6-concierge`, `j12-concierge-2`. Cut reversed on 2026-11-12: the feature is built and shipped in the legacy console, and no measured case showed that removing it is better; how much it is used is counted by the census (MIG-017). Owner decision OD-3.

measured.floor: no slower than the legacy concierge (BL-18).

requirements.title: Atomic owner ledger and causal ecosystem timeline
requirements.statement: Sortyard domain state, append-only audit/event, receipts and outbox commit atomically. Durable order is scoped to its authoritative owner/workspace; cross-service events retain source cursor/sequence, correlation and causal references. Realtime arrival order is not global commit order.
acceptance: AC1: The actual runtime writer cannot update/delete history through direct/transaction/upsert/bulk or table-security changes.
AC2: Identical event identity/content replays once; conflicting content refuses.
AC3: Authorized replay preserves late-visible events or explicitly reports a retention/resync gap.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: State and history are spread over `state.json`, `grooming.json`, the dispatcher's SQLite database, JSONL ledgers and the board's database, with no common order; they have disagreed in production (HARNESS-256; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN; BL-14, BL-24).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: History of any object
requirements.statement: For any object the API returns its events in order, with who, when, before and after.
acceptance: AC1: The current state of a task equals the fold of its events (replay test).
requirements.source: `sortyard.object_history(kind, id)`; harness-console J5.

requirements.title: Read models are projections and say so
requirements.statement:
Aggregates (queue census, throughput windows, dashboards) are computed from the ledger and
state tables, are recomputable at will, store nothing authoritative, and are labelled with
`as_of`. A read model never feeds a scheduling decision.
acceptance: AC1: Dropping and rebuilding every read model changes no API result other than `as_of`.
AC2: A read endpoint causes no write, no Job and no outbound call.
requirements.source: FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN ("The read model is a projection of source records, never a second authority"; "No request body, database write, Job creation, or trace span is caused by these reads").

requirements.title: The metric catalogue
requirements.statement:
Sortyard ships one catalogue in which each metric has an id, an exact definition (numerator,
denominator, clock, window, cohort), a unit and its coverage rule. The v1 catalogue:

| Id | Definition |
|---|---|
| `queue.actionable` | Eligible tasks and admissible stages now, by project and state. Age runs from the release or queued transition to first schedule; open waits use `as_of`. |
| `stage.pickup_latency` | For stages first scheduled in the window: `first_scheduled − eligible_since`, where `eligible_since` is the later of the queued transition and the predecessor's pass. Dependency wait is reported separately and is never called a scheduler delay. |
| `stage.execution` | For attempts terminal in the window: scheduled→running, running→collecting, collecting→terminal. Missing endpoints are counted, not dropped. |
| `chain.outcomes` | Chains that reached a terminal outcome in the window, once each, by outcome (done, parked, handed-back, cancelled), with shares. |
| `chain.cycle_time` | For chains done in the window: done − claimed. Open chains are shown by current age, not included in percentiles. |
| `task.lead_time` | For tasks done in the window: done − created; and time in each board state. |
| `merges` | Change requests merged into a default branch in the window, by host merge time, unique by repo and number. |
| `merge.open_to_first_green` / `merge.green_to_merge` / `merge.open_to_merge` | From the change request's history and its required check runs. |
| `review.rounds` | Reviews with a verdict per task; share of tasks at or over the tripwire. |
| `fix.rounds`, `conflict.rounds` | Per task and per window. |
| `lanes.utilisation` | Slot-seconds held ÷ slot-seconds available, by project; same for each heavy cap. |
| `handback.count`, `park.count` | By reason and blocking-cause kind. |
| `cost.agent_minutes_per_merge` | Agent wall time of every finished stage for a project (builds, reviews, fix rounds, triage, failures) ÷ changes merged in its repos, same window. |
| `cost.stages_per_merge`, `cost.tokens_per_merge` | Same cohort; tokens where recorded. |
| `main.health` | Per repo: latest completed required run on the default branch, its conclusion, and the age of the last success. |
| `chain.control_wait` | For chains terminal in the window: the sum of the gaps between an enabling event and the action it enables (stage finished → next dispatched, checks green → merge armed, verdict → next round, merge observed → Done). Excludes time in agents, CI, reviews and waiting for a slot (FLW-019). |
| `stall.episodes` | Episodes in the window in which a chain passed a phase bound or a stage made no progress: count, share recovered with no person, time to detection, time to recovery (REC-026). |
| `operator.interventions` | Mutations by a person on work in flight (requeue, cancel, force, manual state change, resolving a hand-back), for each week and for each 100 merged tasks; owner-list answers are counted separately (REC-024). |
| `upgrade.impact` | For each upgrade: failed API requests, missed events, time without a leader, stages failed or retried because of it (DEP-010). |
acceptance: AC1: Each metric has a fixture with a hand-computed expected value.
AC2: A metric whose source is incomplete returns `null` with a reason (API-012).
AC3: Percentiles use nearest-rank and state `n`.

AC4: The four comparison metrics (`chain.control_wait`, `stall.episodes`, `operator.interventions`, `upgrade.impact`) have one definition each, shared by the tests that record them from MS3 on and by the catalogue, so a demonstration and a dashboard cannot disagree.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract "Metric definitions"; `metrics/analyze.py` (merged per day, open→first green, last green→merge, open→merge, review rounds, auto-merge use); conductor README `cost_item`.

requirements.title: Throughput windows
requirements.statement:
Catalogue metrics are available per hour, day and week, by project, lane and workflow. Windows
describe the past and gate nothing.
acceptance: AC1: Window boundaries are half-open and in UTC; a record is counted in exactly one window.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.8 ThroughputWindow; Joe 2026-11-05 (time survives only as looking back at throughput).

requirements.title: Delivery cost
requirements.statement:
For each project and window: agent-minutes per merged change and stages per merged change,
computed from recorded stage usage. Stages whose usage is unreadable are named, not guessed.
acceptance: AC1: The published number and the list of excluded stages always appear together.

AC2: Demonstration (ledger, MS7) — agent-minutes and stages for each merged change over the pilot's window, from the ledger, against the same project's legacy figure. Target: no agent-minute is spent on a stage that could not succeed (missing base, unregistered target, unreadable input), and the figure is available for any window and project within 1 s. Floor: cost for each merged change no higher than the legacy baseline, and the figure kept as a series for any past window, which the legacy item cannot give (BL-16).
requirements.source: driver §3 "Delivery cost" (k3s-harness #186: "Unreadable requests are named, not guessed").
requirements.baseline: The sync writes a delivery-cost item on each board for the current window; the cost of a merged change is not kept as a series (conductor README `cost_item`; k3s-harness #186; BL-16).

measured.target: no agent-minute is spent on a stage that could not succeed (missing base, unregistered target, unreadable input), and the figure is available for any window and project within 1 s.
measured.floor: cost for each merged change no higher than the legacy baseline, and the figure kept as a series for any past window, which the legacy item cannot give (BL-16).

requirements.title: Wait versus work
requirements.statement:
For any chain and any window the time is decomposed into: waiting on dependencies, waiting for a
slot, waiting for admission, executing, waiting on CI, waiting on review, waiting on a person.
acceptance: AC1: The components sum to the cycle time within one second.
AC2: Each component maps to reason codes (SCH-009), so the dashboard and the Pickup Preview agree.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract ("Stage timing waterfall and wait-vs-execution decomposition"); FACTORY-STAGE-ATTEMPTS-DESIGN.

requirements.title: Queue census
requirements.statement:
A cheap, bounded endpoint returns current counts: eligible, held by reason, claimed by phase,
stages queued, running and collecting, slots and caps in use. Downstream stages of an open chain
are future work, not queue depth.
acceptance: AC1: The census never counts a stage under a terminal chain as runnable.
requirements.source: `GET /api/mh/queue-census`; FACTORY-DASHBOARD-DESIGN (`eligible_queued_stages` rule).

requirements.title: Daily record
requirements.statement:
One generated record per day and project: what merged, what did not and why, what is parked or
handed back, incidents on main, quarantined jobs, cost. Generated from the ledger; nobody writes
it by hand.
acceptance: AC1: The record for a past day is reproducible byte for byte.

AC2: Demonstration (ledger, MS6) — the daily record is generated twice for 14 past days of the reference workload. Target: byte-identical on every re-run, ready within 60 s of the day's end, with zero model calls. Floor: every figure of the legacy report is present and reproducible, and no agent run is spent writing it (BL-27).
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 13 ("no hand-written status ever again"); JOB-QUARANTINE.md (`ledger/pipeline-daily/YYYY-MM-DD.md`).
requirements.baseline: Throughput reports and Slack cards are written by an agent on a schedule, and the daily pipeline record is a file committed to a repository (driver §6; JOB-QUARANTINE.md; BL-27).

measured.target: byte-identical on every re-run, ready within 60 s of the day's end, with zero model calls.
measured.floor: every figure of the legacy report is present and reproducible, and no agent run is spent writing it (BL-27).

requirements.title: System metrics endpoint
requirements.statement:
Each component serves Prometheus metrics: reconcile duration and lag, claim latency, queue
depth, Job counts by phase, API latency and error rate, database pool use, mirror age, ledger
append rate.
acceptance: AC1: The metric names and labels are documented and covered by a snapshot test.
AC2: Scraping needs no credential beyond network reach, or a token when configured.
requirements.source: inference — the legacy system exposes `/api/health` and OTLP only; the standard for Kubernetes installs is a scrape endpoint.

requirements.title: Structured logs with correlation ids
requirements.statement:
Logs are JSON lines with level, component, request id and — where they apply — project, task,
chain, stage and attempt.
acceptance: AC1: One `grep` by a correlation id — request or task id in MS1, chain id from MS3 — across component logs yields the whole story.
AC2: Error output from child processes is captured, not discarded.
requirements.source: 2026-11-12 release stall ("stderr is discarded, so it was reproduced with a server-side dry run").

requirements.title: OpenTelemetry export
requirements.statement:
Optional export of lifecycle spans over OTLP, with W3C trace context carried from task to chain
to stage. Export uses an outbox with a bounded backlog; drops are counted and reported. The
ledger stays the record: telemetry never overwrites state.
acceptance: AC1: With the collector down, nothing blocks and the gap is visible in health.
requirements.source: `mh.py` trace outbox (notes: trim pending over 5,000, prune delivered after 7 days); OTLP-TRACE-DESIGN; factory-measurement-contract ("Never overwrite authoritative business state with telemetry").

requirements.title: Notifications
requirements.statement:
Routing rules send events to channels (webhook, Slack-compatible webhook, email). Shipped
defaults notify a person only for owner-list items (REC-024) and for a factory-down state with
nothing acting on it. Everything else goes to the pipeline: a task, a condition, a queue.
Notifications are de-duplicated per condition and their delivery is logged.
acceptance: AC1: A red main with an active triage chain sends no notification.
AC2: A notification that could not be delivered is itself a condition after its retry budget.
requirements.source: driver §6 ("Findings go to the pipeline, not to the owner … The stall watch stays quiet about a red that has an active conductor item"); DV40-ALERT-READBACK-DESIGN.

requirements.title: Attention list
requirements.statement:
A computed list of what needs a look now: chains past their phase bound, credentials expiring or
quarantined, red main with nothing acting, silent mechanisms, low quota, open conditions. Each
entry carries its evidence links. An entry can be dismissed with a reason and restored.
acceptance: AC1: The list is the same through API, MCP (`get_attention`) and UI.
AC2: Dismissal is audited and expires when the underlying condition changes.
requirements.source: harness-console J8; API.md "Needs-attention insights (HC-14)"; console calls `/api/insights`, `/dismiss`, `/restore`.

requirements.title: No phone-home
requirements.statement:
Sortyard sends nothing to its authors or any third party. There is no usage telemetry in 1.0;
any later telemetry is opt-in and documented field by field.
acceptance: AC1: A network-policy test runs the full scenario suite with egress limited to the configured Git host and model provider.
requirements.source: Plane benchmark (instance telemetry defaults to enabled).

requirements.title: Retention
requirements.statement:
Retention is configuration with documented defaults: ledger events (keep), traces and stage
logs (90 days), run directories (REC-022), webhook delivery logs (30 days). Expiry is a
registered mechanism.
acceptance: AC1: Expired blobs are removed and their references say "expired", not "missing".
requirements.source: `mh.py` retention (notes); DESIGN §3.6 `retention` policy kind (parameters left open in the frozen schema).

requirements.title: Main-branch release health
requirements.statement:
Per repo: the latest completed required run on the default branch and the age of the last
success. A failing required run is a factory-down signal until a later success; an owner-accepted
hold changes its disposition, not its colour.
acceptance: AC1: Green change-request checks never dilute this state.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract "Mainline release health".

requirements.title: Improvement ledger
requirements.statement:
A record for each tuning intervention with hypothesis, pre and post cohort values and a verdict
(`improved`, `regressed`, `inconclusive`, `not_live`). Deferred past 1.0 on the evidence that
the estate's ledger of this kind is not in regular use; the cut is conditional on the usage
census (MIG-017), and the scorecard (QLT-051) already records before and after values for every
measured criterion.
acceptance: AC1: Until it ships, the audit of policy changes (SCH-011) plus the windowed metrics give the raw material.
requirements.source: factory-measurement-contract "Sense → respond → improve loop".

requirements.title: Versioned meta-harness resources
requirements.statement: Archetypes, workflows, workflow roles/personas, skills, context recipes, quality bars, eval packs, integration definitions and policy references are first-class versioned resources. Immutable content/version is separate from mutable assignments and activation; newest published content is not automatically active.
acceptance: AC1: Publishing identical content is idempotent; a published version cannot change.
AC2: A project pins and explicitly adopts an archetype/skill/workflow version.
AC3: Candidate policy/definition publication alone does not activate it.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: One owner and one write route per resource family
requirements.statement: Each family has a registered authoritative owner and epoch. Sortyard owns its native domain; existing policy service, Git definitions and partner product records remain authoritative until an explicit family handover. Appwrite materializations are labelled read projections when the owner is external.
acceptance: AC1: Editing a projection uses the owner command or is refused.
AC2: Source hashes/versions and observation freshness remain visible.
AC3: No successful command is inferred from a local projection update.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: Project configuration is `repos.yaml`, read from a Git clone on every pass. A failed clone made a pass order by priority alone (task-pickup conformance row 3, HARNESS-255); since 2026-11-10 an invalid entry is dropped for the pass (kept as RDY-013). Caps and thresholds are not configuration at all (BL-22, BL-10).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Git-managed definitions with an API proposal path
requirements.statement: A definition assignment may be source-locked to a reviewed Git ref. Both UI and delegated agents can propose a managed change through the same API; ordinary review/CI/GitOps publishes it. A read-only materialization does not eliminate the operator command surface.
acceptance: AC1: Source-lock refuses direct version/activation mutation.
AC2: A proposal links its task/change request and eventual published version.
AC3: A failed pull preserves the last accepted version and reports freshness.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: The conductor reads `repos.yaml` from a Git clone on every pass, so a merged change is in force within one pass with no further step; a failed clone degraded a pass (HARNESS-255; BL-10, BL-22).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Pinned execution context and explicit live policy resolution
requirements.statement: A binding pins workflow, role/persona, skill and context-packet versions. Each runtime policy decision records the exact effective policy family/variant/version, snapshot, reason and fallback used at that decision point. Updating a definition does not silently rewrite an active stage packet.
acceptance: AC1: A recipe/skill edit leaves an existing packet hash unchanged.
AC2: A later policy decision identifies its actual policy versions.
AC3: Explicit emergency revocation is governed and audited separately.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Policy consumers and declared defaults
requirements.statement: Tunables are registered decision points with documented defaults, owner source/version, scope resolution and consumer support. The legacy constant inventory is a migration input to re-observe; it is not evidence that every old literal is the current policy.
acceptance: AC1: A policy with no supported consumer is visibly ineffective at that decision point.
AC2: Conflicting equal-rank variants return a named conflict rather than an arbitrary winner.
AC3: Missing source uses only the declared absent-state rule and records its fallback.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Definitions are validated when applied
requirements.statement:
`apply` validates schema and meaning and refuses with a message naming the definition and the
rule: an unbounded phase (REC-001), a gate with no absent-state (FLW-009), a stage that breaks
pipeline purity (FLW-001), a reference to a missing template or profile, a threshold outside its
allowed range.
acceptance: AC1: `apply --validate` runs the same checks without writing and is usable in CI.
AC2: A partially valid bundle applies nothing.
requirements.source: meta-harness tradition of script refusals (DESIGN §3.6 "prose rule → script refusal"); `repos_check.py`.

requirements.title: See the effect before saving
requirements.statement:
Changing a policy, lane or project setting shows a diff and a what-if: how the Pickup Preview
would differ.
acceptance: AC1: The what-if uses the scheduler's own evaluator with the proposed values.
requirements.source: DESIGN §6 view 7 (simulate); UI-008.

requirements.title: A default bundle ships with every release
requirements.statement:
Each release carries a default bundle: the `change` and `job` workflows, their packet templates,
the review checklists, harness profiles for the shipped harnesses, and default policies. A fresh
install applies it. On upgrade, changed defaults are offered as a diff the operator accepts; an
installation's edits are never overwritten. An installation may layer its own bundle on top; the
estate's does, and keeps the legacy settings that are not defaults for strangers (MIG-010).
acceptance: AC1: A fresh install can run the demo with no definition authored by the user.
AC2: An upgrade never changes behaviour by silently replacing a definition the operator edited.
requirements.source: `definitions/seed/` (9 workflows, 4 roles, 2 archetypes, 4 context recipes, 8 lanes, 10 policies — to be re-cut to the kinds in DEF-001); CORPUS M1.2.

requirements.title: Onboarding a project is one object and one check
requirements.statement:
A project is onboarded by creating it with its repositories, lanes, build and release switches.
An onboarding check then verifies and reports: the landing credential can push; auto-merge is
allowed; at least one required check exists (or the plain-git adapter is chosen); the mirror is
created. Claims start only when the check passes.
acceptance: AC1: A project whose check fails shows exactly which item failed and stays unbuilt.
AC2: Onboarding needs no edit to any file outside Sortyard.
requirements.source: onboarding.md (one `repos.yaml` entry; the onboarding check; "GitHub requirements per repo"); SY-DEC-003 (registration sequence: build registry first, driver last).

requirements.title: Versioned extension registry with isolated execution
requirements.statement: Skills, archetype/workflow/eval packs, sensors and API integrations have registry entries, compatibility/capability metadata, owners and per-project assignments. Extensions execute through versioned definitions, isolated containers or governed HTTP adapters; they do not load arbitrary code inside the control plane.
acceptance: AC1: A compatible skill pack can be registered and assigned without a control-plane image change.
AC2: Missing tools, credentials or compatibility block binding with a named reason.
AC3: Installation cannot silently widen a project/worker grant.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: Every new behaviour of the legacy system — a check, a sensor, a workflow step — is a change to the conductor's code and a release of its bundle. Releases were manual, and the release controller that followed was blocked for about 32 minutes on 2026-11-12 (task-pickup conformance row 8, HARNESS-246; BL-11, BL-10).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Worker image contract and conformance kit
requirements.statement:
The stage contract (EXE-006) is published with a conformance kit: a container that plays the
controller's side against a candidate worker image and reports pass or fail per clause. The
shipped harness images pass it in CI.
acceptance: AC1: A third party can build a harness image and verify it with one command and no Sortyard install.
requirements.source: CORPUS M5.7 (conformance test kit); EXE-012.

requirements.title: Git host adapters
requirements.statement:
Everything Sortyard needs from a Git host is one interface: fetch, push a branch, open or update
a change request, read its state and checks, arm and disarm auto-merge, comment, read protection
rules, mint a read-only token. 1.0 ships `plain-git` and `github`.
acceptance: AC1: The scenario suite is written against the interface and runs on both a fake and `plain-git`.
AC2: A capability an adapter lacks is declared, and dependent features say so (plain-git has no hosted checks, so CIH features are inactive).
requirements.source: DESIGN §5.2 ("GitHub Issues and Linear … integrations, never dependencies"); AGENTS.md "pipeline purity".

requirements.title: Sensors are scheduled jobs that call the API
requirements.statement:
A sensor is a container run on a schedule by the same Job machinery as stages, in its own lane
outside the delivery pipeline, with a sensor token. It files findings and heartbeats through the
API. Sensors may reach live systems; delivery stages may not.
acceptance: AC1: A sensor's schedule is a registered mechanism with a freshness window (REC-017).
AC2: A finding is de-duplicated by a stable key: repeats update its last-seen time.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.7 (Sensor), §1.4; factory-measurement-contract ("repeat sweeps update age instead of duplicating incidents").

requirements.title: Bundles from a repository at a pinned ref
requirements.statement:
`apply` accepts a Git URL and a commit or tag; the bundle's source and content hash are recorded
on every version it creates.
acceptance: AC1: An unpinned ref (a branch name) is refused unless explicitly allowed.
requirements.source: DESIGN §3.7 (registry "git-backed in v1"); CORPUS M3.2.

requirements.title: Tracker import adapters
requirements.statement:
Importing from an external tracker is an interface with one shipped implementation (Plane):
list projects, items, relations, states, order and comments read-only.
acceptance: AC1: The adapter holds a read-only credential and issues only read requests (asserted by the HTTP fake).
requirements.source: `src/sortyard/shadow/sources.py` (GET only; refuses redirects that would carry the key elsewhere); MIG-003.

requirements.title: Contracts are versioned
requirements.statement:
The stage contract, the adapter interfaces and the bundle format carry versions. A release
states which versions it supports; a contract version is supported for at least two minor
releases after its successor ships.
acceptance: AC1: A worker image built for the previous contract version still runs on the current release.
requirements.source: DESIGN §11.2 ("an API-stability/versioning commitment").

requirements.title: Small control plane on the existing substrate
requirements.statement: A Helm package installs API/UI, controller and fenced integrator as needed plus ephemeral worker Jobs. Appwrite is an explicit existing/separately operated substrate prerequisite. The migration source Postgres remains only until accepted migration; the package does not silently install another Appwrite estate.
acceptance: AC1: Rendered target architecture includes no default second application SQL database.
AC2: Each workload has a clear privilege boundary.
AC3: Current Postgres chart behavior is labelled implementation baseline until the adapter ships.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: The delivery system is a Plane installation, the dispatcher API, the conductor's CronJobs, a release controller, a mechanism-health job, host crons and a tools pod. `mechanisms.yaml` registers 68 mechanisms across the estate; the pipeline's share is counted by the baseline capture (BL-14).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Installable by a namespace admin
requirements.statement:
The chart needs no CustomResourceDefinitions and no cluster-scoped objects by default. Optional
cluster-scoped extras (a PriorityClass, a second namespace for workers) are flags, each
documented with what is lost without it.
acceptance: AC1: `helm install` succeeds with a ServiceAccount that has admin on one namespace only.
AC2: From MS3, when the controller ships: its Role is limited to Jobs, Pods, Pods/log, ConfigMaps and Secrets in the worker namespace.

AC3: Demonstration (drill, MS3) — a release that adds a workload and a permission is installed by upgrade with a namespace-admin account, on a fresh install and on an upgraded one. Target: one `helm upgrade`, zero objects applied by hand, the controller's Role rendered by the chart. Floor: no release needs an object applied by hand; the legacy release of 2026-11-12 did (BL-11).
requirements.source: 2026-11-12 release stall (a new CronJob could not be applied because a hand-maintained Role did not name it); `k8s/mh-rbac.yaml`.
requirements.baseline: The legacy RBAC is a hand-maintained Role. On 2026-11-12 a new CronJob could not be applied because the Role did not name it, and the release stalled for about 32 minutes (release note 2026-11-12; `k8s/mh-rbac.yaml`; BL-11).

measured.target: one `helm upgrade`, zero objects applied by hand, the controller's Role rendered by the chart.
measured.floor: no release needs an object applied by hand; the legacy release of 2026-11-12 did (BL-11).

requirements.title: Appwrite application state and private artifacts
requirements.statement: Use Appwrite native rows/transactions for Sortyard-owned state, ledger, receipts and outbox and private Storage for large content. External product data remains with its owner. Blob upload is verified before database metadata publication and reconciled on interruption.
acceptance: AC1: State/event/receipt/outbox commit together within the supported transaction budget.
AC2: A failed upload or metadata commit never advertises an incomplete artifact as ready.
AC3: Partner-store unavailability does not cause an independent writable copy.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.baseline: State is in `state.json` and `grooming.json` on a volume, the dispatcher's SQLite database, JSONL ledgers, a shared work volume, and the board's own database and services (BL-14).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Supported self-hosted Appwrite profile
requirements.statement: The default profile targets the verified self-hosted Appwrite version/capabilities and compatible SDK. Setup explicitly provisions a dedicated logical project and least-privilege schema/runtime identities through the estate custody route. Hybrid SQL requires a demonstrated unsupported invariant.
acceptance: AC1: Qualification checks server/SDK compatibility and configured transaction limits.
AC2: Runtime lacks schema/admin and broad resource-bypass API keys.
AC3: A distinct installation cannot read another application project.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Install time
requirements.statement:
From a clean cluster with the prerequisites present, one command installs a running Sortyard and
prints its address and the setup token; one more runs the demo. Both paths are scripted and
timed in CI on every release candidate, using published artefacts only.
acceptance: AC1: Install to first task filed, on the reference runner and a kind cluster. Target: one command and 3 minutes. Floor: 8 commands and 15 minutes, with no step that requires editing a file.
AC2: Install to the demo chain finished. Target: one more command and 5 minutes more. Floor: 30 minutes in total.
AC3: The CI job fails when a floor is missed and writes the measured times to the scorecard (QLT-051).
AC4: The comparison with the estate is recorded once: what a second installation of the legacy system needs (BL-13) beside the measured install.
requirements.source: DESIGN §1.9 ("`helm install` it on a fresh cluster in an afternoon") — tightened; DESIGN §0 (standing the legacy system up elsewhere means about six repositories, a jump box and a private network); goldfish GF1-05 (no prerequisite check, no one-command replica).

measured.target: one command and 3 minutes.
measured.floor: 8 commands and 15 minutes, with no step that requires editing a file.

measured.target: one more command and 5 minutes more.
measured.floor: 30 minutes in total.

requirements.title: Explicit substrate and connector setup
requirements.statement: Configuration names the Appwrite endpoint/logical project, supported version, custody references, required indexed schema, canonical origins and registered connectors. Setup identifies missing capabilities; no secret values enter ordinary config objects or public health.
acceptance: AC1: A missing project/grant/index is actionable rather than an empty successful install.
AC2: A small core install needs no Ranker/Closer/Walwarden deployment to run unrelated work.
AC3: Values are schema-checked and provider credentials stay in their existing custody.
requirements.source: `charts/sortyard/values.yaml`; Plane benchmark (58 variables in the self-host env file).
requirements.amendment_reason: Latest owner scope, single-authority integration and existing testing/governance doctrine

requirements.title: Versioned Appwrite schema evolution
requirements.statement: Provision indexed columns, permissions and schema versions with supported Appwrite APIs. Released data mappings are immutable; changes follow compatible expansion then contraction. Index readiness is part of readiness. The old SQL migrations remain accurate only for the retained source store.
acceptance: AC1: Previous and next application readers work during an additive change.
AC2: A newer unsupported schema or missing index fails readiness.
AC3: Migration interruption resumes from durable checkpoints without changing published historical content.
requirements.source: Owner control-plane requirements, 2026-11-15 America/New_York; SY-DEC-004; company/INTENTS.md I1/I3/I5 and BIG-PICTURE.md (source date 2026-11-16).
requirements.amendment_reason: Reconciled with current owner direction and substrate/authority contracts

requirements.title: Upgrade guarantees
requirements.statement:
From 1.0: any 1.x upgrades directly to any later 1.y; this is tested in CI from the last patch
of every earlier minor, with data. Rolling back the application by one minor without restoring
the database is supported. Before 1.0: each 0.x upgrades from 0.(x−1), tested, with any
exception in the upgrade notes.
acceptance: AC1: The upgrade matrix job seeds data with the old version, upgrades, and runs the new version's scenario suite.
